prompt: A function is O(n²). Which of these three versions of that fact is written correctly for a non-technical stakeholder who just wants to know if a page will feel slow?
choices: "The page will stay fast at today's file sizes. If someone uploads a much bigger file than usual, it will get noticeably slower, and it slows down faster than you'd expect as the file grows — we already have a fix queued."
"dedupe_rows is O(n^2) because it rescans the whole kept-list per row; swapping the inner list for a set brings it to O(n)."
"There were some performance issues that might possibly affect page load in certain situations."
"The algorithm's time complexity is quadratic with respect to input cardinality, which is suboptimal relative to a linearithmic or linear bound."

prompt: An incident summary spends its first three paragraphs describing what was checked and ruled out before finally stating, in the fourth paragraph, how long the outage lasted and what caused it. What should change to apply "lead with the answer"?
choices: Move a one- or two-sentence summary of impact and root cause to the very top, keeping the chronological investigation detail afterward for readers who want it
Delete the chronological investigation detail entirely, since a good incident summary never includes it
Nothing — incident summaries should always be told in the order the investigation actually happened, since that's the most honest account
Add more hedging language to the opening paragraph so readers aren't misled before the full timeline is explained
